484:
This chapter applies to contracts for the procurement of equipment, supplies, services, construction, professional and consultant services solicited or entered into by the city after the effective date unless the parties agree to its application to a contract solicited or entered into prior to the effective date.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
485:
This chapter repeals all previously issued ordinances, rules or regulations pertaining to public procurement for this city.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
486:
This chapter shall become effective at 12:01 a.m. on October 1, 1994.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
487:
(1) Contract file: All determinations and other written records pertaining to the solicitation, award or performance of a contract or purchase order shall be maintained by the city in a contract file by the purchasing agent.
(2) Retention of procurement records: All procurement records shall be retained and disposed of by the city in accordance with records retention guidelines and schedules approved by the city council. If a contract is being funded in whole or in part by assistance from a federal agency, then all procurement records pertaining to that contract shall be maintained for three (3) years from the closeout date of the assistance agreement or the final disposition of any controversy arising out of the assistance agreement.
(3) Public access: Procurement information shall be a public record to the extent required by the laws of the State of Georgia, with the exception that privileged and confidential commercial or financial information obtained in response to a request for proposals shall not be disclosed.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
488:
When the procurement transaction involves the expenditure of federal assistance or contract funds, the procurement transaction shall be conducted in accordance with any applicable mandatory federal law and authorized regulations which are not reflected in this chapter. Notwithstanding federal requirements, where federal assistance or contract funds are used in a procurement, requirements of this Code that are more restrictive than federal requirements shall be followed.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
492:
(1) Principal public purchasing official: Except as otherwise provided herein, the purchasing agent shall serve as the principal public purchasing official for the city and shall be responsible for the procurement of equipment, supplies, services, construction, and professional or consultant services in accordance with this chapter, as well as the management and disposal of supplies.
(2) Duties: In accordance with this chapter, and subject to the supervision of the city manager, the purchasing agent shall:
(a) Procure or supervise the procurement of all equipment, supplies, services, construction, and professional or consultant services needed by the city;
(b) Exercise direct supervision over the city's central stores and general supervision over all other inventories of supplies belonging to this city;
(c) Sell, trade or otherwise dispose of surplus equipment or supplies belonging to the city as authorized in this Code section or in section 4-3707 of this Code; and
(d) Establish and maintain programs for development of specifications and administer, inspect, and accept contracts in cooperation with the using department.
(3) Operational procedures: Consistent with this chapter, the purchasing agent shall adopt operational procedures relating to the execution of his or her duties. All operating procedures shall be approved by the city manager and adopted by the city council. These operating procedures shall be set forth in a purchasing manual and shall be consistent with financial reporting requirements as provided by this Code.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
493:
(1) Purchasing agent: Except as provided herein, the purchasing agent shall have the authority to solicit and recommend contracts for the procurement of all equipment, supplies, services, construction, and professional or consultant services for the city.
(2) Purchasing staff. Under the authority of the purchasing agent, the purchasing staff shall execute responsibilities at all bid openings which shall include coordination of clock calibration with the National Bureau of Standards, stamp all bids received, and any subsequent responsibilities as specified prior to and after all bid openings.
(3) Other city officers or employees: With the approval of the city manager, the purchasing agent may delegate authority to purchase certain equipment, supplies, services, or construction items to other city officials, if such delegation is deemed necessary for the procurement of those items. Any unauthorized action shall result in disciplinary action by the city manager.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
494:
(1) Relationship with using departments: The purchasing agent shall maintain a close and cooperative relationship with the using departments. The purchasing agent shall afford each using department agency reasonable opportunity to participate in and make recommendations regarding procurement matters affecting the using department. When in consultation with the using department regarding a procurement, the purchasing agent, to the extent practicable, shall use every effort to reach an agreement with the using departments.
(2) Requisitions: All departments, with the authority of the director of the department, shall file with the purchasing agent detailed requisitions or estimates of their requirements of equipment, supplies, services, construction, professional or consultant services, in such manner and at such times and for future periods as the purchasing agent shall prescribe in writing including the following:
(a) Unforeseen requirements: A using department may file with the purchasing agent at any time a requisition or estimate for any equipment, supplies, services, construction, professional or consultant services, the need for which was unforeseen or not anticipated when the above-detailed estimates were filed; and
(b) Revisory power of purchasing agent: The purchasing agent shall examine each requisition or estimate and shall have the authority to revise it as to quantity, quality or estimated cost; provided, that the needs of the departments are met and revisions as to quality and quantity shall be made in accordance with standards and specifications established pursuant to this chapter.
(3) Estimates: All departments shall file with the purchasing agent, within thirty (30) days after the adoption of the annual budget and quarterly, thereafter, estimates of their needs for the procurement of equipment, supplies, services, construction, and professional or consultant services for the ensuing fiscal year or calendar quarter. The purchasing agent shall utilize such estimates for the scheduling of work activities and of procurements to be made by the purchasing agent. The purchasing agent shall compile and consolidate all estimates of supplies needed by the departments to determine total requirements of a given commodity.
(4) List of authorized signatures: All heads of departments shall provide the purchasing agent annually with a list of signatures of persons in the department who are authorized to sign requisitions on behalf of the department.
(5) Examination of contracts: The purchasing agent and the head of the department shall examine all contracts to determine the accuracy of the substance and the inclusion of required bonds and certificates of insurance.
(6) Receiving reports: The department shall deliver receiving reports to the city treasurer and to the purchasing agent upon receipt of supplies procured under city contracts.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
495:
The purchasing agent shall have the authority to enter into and sign contracts on behalf of the city, pursuant to section 4-3203 of the Code of the City of East Point, in the following circumstances:
(1) For the purchase of supplies of every type and description and contracts which take the form of purchase orders where the city council has authorized the purchase in the normal course of the budget process, without further authorization by the city council.
Provided, that the purchasing agent complies with all other requirements of this chapter.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95; Ord. No. 011-03, § 1, 3-3-03)
496:
All contracts, letters of engagement or agreements for equipment, supplies, services, construction services, professional services and consultant services resulting from the bid/procurement process must be approved by council before being executed by the purchasing agent and mayor. Council will approve such contract if they meet the scope of work bid out and the price of the accepted bid.
(Ord. No. 011-03, § 1, 3-3-03)
500:
(1) Conditions for use: Contracts or purchase orders shall be awarded by competitive sealed bidding except as otherwise provided in section 4-3301 (Methods of source selection).
(2) Invitations for bids: An invitation for bids shall be issued and shall include a purchase description and all contractual terms and conditions applicable to the procurement.
(3) Public notice: Where the estimated contract is in excess of twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000.00), an advertisement inviting bids shall be published at least once a week for two (2) consecutive weeks, in at least one (1) newspaper of general circulation in the city, at least fourteen (14) days preceding the date set for receipt of bids. Notice of bid security, if required, shall be included in the public notice. The public notice shall contain a general description of the equipment, supplies, services, construction, and professional or consultant services to be procured and shall state the location of where appropriate solicitation documents may be obtained, and the time and place of opening of solicitation documents.
(4) Bidders' list: The issuance of a public notice shall not be required where the estimated amount
of the contract does not exceed twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000.00) and the purchasing agent has established and maintains a current bidders' list. The bidders' list must contain more than an adequate number of vendors with the capacity to furnish the service or supplies required. Further, the list shall constitute a reasonable representation of all prospective vendors in the market place.
(5) Clock calibration: Prior to all bid openings, the purchasing agent or staff shall coordinate the clock calibration used in the bid process, with the National Bureau of Standards.
(6) Bid opening: Bids shall be opened publicly in the presence of one (1) or more witnesses at the time and place designated in the invitation for bids. The name of each bidder, the amount of each bid, and such other relevant information as the purchasing agent deems appropriate shall be recorded. The record and each bid shall be open to public inspection.
(7) Bid acceptance: Bids shall be unconditionally accepted without alteration or correction, except as authorized in this chapter; provided, that the bids are delivered to the purchasing agent at the time, place and under the conditions contained in the invitation for bids.
(8) Bid evaluation: Bids shall be evaluated based on the requirements set forth in the invitation for bids. The criteria that will affect the bid price and be considered in evaluation for award shall be objectively measurable, such as discounts, transportation costs, and total or life cycle costs. The invitation for bids shall set forth the evaluation criteria to be used including but not limited to inspection, testing, quality, workmanship, delivery, and suitability for a particular purpose. No criteria may be used in bid evaluation that are not set forth in the invitation for bids.
(9) Correction or withdrawal of bids:
(a) Before bid opening: Correction or withdrawal of bids may be allowed by the purchasing agent before the scheduled time and date of bid opening. The bidder may withdraw the bid, without revealing the amount of the bid, by submitting a new sealed bid or providing written notice of withdrawal before bid opening. Notice of withdrawal must be received by the purchasing agent prior to bid opening.
(b) After bid opening: Mistakes or errors in bids discovered by the purchasing agent or bidder after bid opening may be corrected or withdrawal of bids may be allowed, in accordance with this section. A bidder who discovers a mistake or error in the bid may request relief from the purchasing agent; and the purchasing agent may allow relief as prescribed below:
(i) Clerical mistakes: Any obvious clerical mistake, including but not limited to an error in price extension, placement of decimal points, reversal of prices, FOB destination, or FOB point of origination may be corrected by the purchasing agent after written verification is made by the bidder.
(ii) Corrections: A written determination is made that the following conditions are met:
1. Evidence of the mistake and the bid intended is clear and convincing on the face of the bid; and
2. The bid received and as actually intended is the lowest responsive bid received.
Provided, that if there is no clear and convincing evidence, the bidder shall not be permitted to withdraw the bid without prejudice or to correct the error; and upon failure to enter into contract, such bidder shall forfeit the bid security.
(iii) Withdrawal: If there is a significant and obvious disparity between the prices of the lowest bidder and of the other bidders, a bidder may be permitted to withdraw without prejudice, upon submission of evidence that a nonintentional error occurred. Provided, that a withdrawal of bid shall not be allowed without prejudice unless clear and convincing evidence exists to support the error.
(10) Tie bids: In the event two (2) or more bidders are tied in price while otherwise meeting all of the required conditions, the contract shall be awarded to a bidder whose principal place of business is within the city.
(11) Award: The contract shall be awarded with reasonable promptness by written notice to the lowest responsible and responsive bidder whose bid meets the requirements and criteria set forth in the invitation for bids. Provided, however, that the city reserves the right to reject all bids. In the event all bids exceed available funds as certified by the city treasurer, and the low responsive bid does not exceed such funds by more than five (5) percent, the purchasing agent is authorized, when time or economic considerations preclude resolicitation of work of a reduced scope, to negotiate an adjustment of the bid price, including changes in the bid requirements, with the low responsible and responsive bidder in order to bring the bid within the amount of available funds.
(12) Multistep sealed bidding: When it is considered impractical to initially prepare a purchase description to support an award based on price, an invitation for bids may be issued requesting the submission of unpriced offers to be followed by an invitation for bids limited to those bidders whose offers have been qualified under the criteria set forth in the first solicitation.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
501:
(1) Conditions for use: When the purchasing agent determines that the use of competitive sealed bidding is neither practicable nor advantageous to the city, a contract may be entered into by the use of the competitive sealed proposals method.
(2) Request for proposals: Proposals shall be solicited through a request for proposals.
(3) Public notice: Public notice of the request for proposals shall be given in the same manner as provided in section 4-3302(3) (Competitive sealed bidding, public notice).
(4) Proposal opening: Proposals shall be publicly opened, and only the names of the offerors shall be disclosed at the opening. Contents of competing offerors' proposals shall not be disclosed during the process of negotiation. Proposals shall be open for public inspection only after contract award. Proprietary or confidential information marked as such in each proposal shall not be disclosed without written consent of the offeror.
(5) Evaluation factors: The request for proposals shall state the relative importance of evaluation factors.
(6) Discussion with responsible offerors and revisions to proposals: Discussions may be conducted with responsible offerors who submit proposals determined to be reasonably susceptible of being selected for award for the purpose of clarification to assure full understanding of and responsiveness to the solicitation requirements. Offerors shall be accorded fair and equal treatment with respect to any opportunity for discussion and revision of proposals, and such revisions may be permitted after submissions and prior to the deadline for submission for the purpose of obtaining best and final offers. In conducting discussions, there shall be no disclosure of information derived from proposals submitted by competing offerors.
(7) Award: Award shall be made to the responsible offeror whose proposal is determined in writing to be the most advantageous to the city, taking into consideration the evaluation factors set forth in the request for proposals. No other factors or criteria shall be used in the evaluation. The contract file shall contain the basis on which the award was made.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
502:
(1) General procedures: Any contract or purchase order for equipment, supplies, services and construction not exceeding twelve thousand five hundred dollars ($12,500.00) may be made without public notice in accordance with small purchase procedures adopted by the purchasing agent in accordance with this chapter. Contract requirements shall not be artificially divided so as to constitute a small purchase under this section. To the extent possible, said purchases shall be made from the vendors on the current bidders' list maintained by the purchasing agent pursuant to section 4-3302(4) of this chapter.
(2) Small purchases under two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500.00): The purchasing agent shall adopt operational procedures for making small purchases of up to two thousand-five hundred dollars ($2,500.00) or less by authorized persons other than the purchasing staff. Such operational procedures shall provide for obtaining adequate and reasonable competition for the equipment, supply, service, or construction being purchased. Further, such operational procedures shall require the preparation and maintenance of written records adequate to document the competition obtained, properly account for the funds expended, and facilitate an audit of the small purchase made.
(3) Competitive quotations: Contracts or purchases for amounts equaling twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000.00) or less may be authorized by the purchasing agent for equipment, supplies, services, or minor construction, through the use of competitive quotations. Quotations of this nature may be oral or written, however, the company name, telephone number, and contact person for all competitive parties shall be made available as a bid record for scrutiny, and must meet the test of sections 4-3320(2) (Contract audit) and section 4-3321 (Reporting anti-competitive practices).
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95; Ord. No. 034-015, 8-17-15)
503:
A contract may be awarded without competition when the purchasing agent determines in writing, after conducting a good faith review of available sources, that there is only one (1) source for the required equipment, supply, service, construction item or professional or consultant service. The purchasing agent shall conduct negotiations, as appropriate, as to price, delivery and terms. A record of sole source procurements shall be maintained that lists each contractor's name, the name and type of each contract, a listing of the item(s) procured under each contract, and the identification number of each contract file.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
504:
Notwithstanding any other provisions of this chapter, where the purchasing agent determines that an emergency exists, the purchasing agent may make or authorize others to make emergency procurements or equipment, supplies, services, construction items or professional or consultant services when the purchasing agent determines there exists a threat to public health, welfare or safety under emergency conditions. Such emergency procurements shall be made with as much competition as is practicable under the circumstances. A written determination of the basis for the emergency and for the selection of the particular contractor shall be included in the contract file. As soon as practicable, a record of each emergency procurement shall be made and shall set forth the contractor's name, the amount and type of the contract, a listing of the item(s) procured under the contract, and the identification number of the contract file.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
506:
An invitation for bids, a request for proposals, or other solicitation may be canceled, or any or all bids or proposals may be rejected in whole or in part as may be specified in the solicitation, when it is for good cause and in the best interest of the city. The reasons therefor shall be made part of the contract file. Each solicitation issued by the city shall state that the solicitation may be cancelled and that any bid or proposal may be rejected in whole or in part for good cause when in the best interest of the city. Notice of cancellation shall be sent to all businesses solicited. The notice shall identify the solicitation, explain the reasons for cancellation, and, where appropriate, explain that opportunity be given to compete on any resolicitation or any future procurements of similar items.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
507:
(1) Determination of responsibility: Responsibility of the bidder or offeror shall be ascertained for each contract awarded by the city based upon full disclosure to the purchasing agent concerning capacity to meet the terms of the contract and based upon past record of performance of similar contracts.
(2) Determination of nonresponsibility: If a bidder or offeror who otherwise would have been awarded a contract is found nonresponsible, a written determination of nonresponsibility setting forth the basis of the finding shall be prepared by the purchasing agent. The unreasonable failure of a bidder or offeror to supply prompt information in connection with an inquiry with respect to responsibility may be grounds for a determination of nonresponsibility. A copy of the determination shall be sent to the nonresponsible bidder or offeror. The final determination shall be made part of the contract file and be made a public record.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
508:
(1) Requirement for bid security: Bid security shall be required for all competitive sealed bidding for contracts for supplies and services when the price is estimated by the purchasing agent to exceed one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000.00). Bid security shall be a bond provided by a surety company authorized to do business in the State of Georgia, or the equivalent in cash, cashier's check or certified check. Nothing herein prevents the requirement of such bonds on contracts for supplies and services under one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000.00) when the purchasing agent determines that the circumstances warrant such requirement.
(2) Amount of bid security: Bid security shall be in an amount equal to at least five (5) percent of the amount of the bid. Unsuccessful bidders shall be entitled to the return of the bid security. Upon failure of a successful bidder to enter into a contract within ten (10) days after the purchasing agent tenders the proposed contract, the bidder shall forfeit the bid security.
(3) Rejection of bids for noncompliance with the bid security requirement: When the invitation for bids requires security, the bid shall be rejected if the purchasing agent determines that the bid fails to comply in a substantial manner with the security requirements.
(4) Withdrawal of bids: If a bidder is permitted to withdraw its bid before the deadline for submission as provided in section 4-3302(9)(a) (Competitive sealed bidding, correction or withdrawal of bids), no action shall be had against the bidder or bid security.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
509:
(1) When required amounts: When a contract for supplies or services is awarded in excess of one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000.00) (or when a contract for professional or consultant services is awarded and the purchasing agent determines that the circumstances so warrant), the following bonds or security shall be delivered to the city and shall become binding on the parties upon the execution of the contract:
(a) A performance bond satisfactory to the city, executed by a surety company authorized to do business in the State of Georgia or otherwise secured in a manner satisfactory to the city, in an amount equal to one hundred (100) percent of the price specified in the contract; and
(b) A payment bond satisfactory to the city, executed by a surety company authorized to do business in the State of Georgia or otherwise secured in a manner satisfactory to the city, for the protection of all persons supplying labor and material to the contractor or its subcontractor for the performance of the work provided for in the contract. The bond shall be in an amount equal to one hundred (100) percent of the price specified in the contract.
(2) Reduction or waiver of bond: The purchasing agent is authorized to reduce or waive performance and payment bonds for contracts for equipment, supplies and services for one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000.00) or less, when the purchasing agent makes a written determination that it is in the best interests of the city to do so. Nothing herein prevents the requirement of such bonds on supply or service contracts under one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000.00) when the circumstances warrant. The purchasing agent is authorized to reduce or waive payment bonds on contracts for professional or consultant services when the purchasing agent determines it is in the best interests of the city.
(3) Authority to require additional bonds: Nothing in this section shall be construed to limit the authority of the city to require a performance or payment bond or other security in addition to those bonds, or in circumstances other than those specified in subsections (1) and (2) of this section.
(4) Suits on payment bonds right to institute: Any person who has furnished labor or material to the contractor for the work provided in the contract, for which a payment bond is furnished under this section, and who had not been paid in full within ninety (90) days from the date on which that person performed the last of the labor or supplied the material, shall have the right to sue on the payment bond for any amount unpaid at the time the suit is instituted and to prosecute the action for the amount due that person.
(5) Suits on payment bonds where and when brought: Every suit instituted upon a payment bond shall be brought in a court of competent jurisdiction for the county or district in which the contract for equipment, supplies, services, construction, and professional or consultant services was to be performed; but no such suit shall be commenced after the expiration of one (1) year after the day on which the last of the labor was performed or material was supplied by the person bringing suit. The obligee named in the bond need not be joined as a party of any such suit.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
511:
(1) When required: The purchasing agent, in consultation with the using department, may determine that it shall be in the best interests of the city to prequalify suppliers for particular types of equipment, supplies, services, construction, and professional or consultant services. Prequalification standards may be imposed by the purchasing agent which must be met by any contractor in order to qualify to respond to an invitation for bids or a request for proposals. Contractors shall be required to submit information to the purchasing agent to assure a fair and impartial determination of whether a contractor has met such prequalifications standards. When prequalification is required, only those contractors who submit the required prequalification information and who are actually prequalified to submit a bid or proposal on the contract in question, or who are parties to a joint venture formed by contractors who are prequalified under this section, shall be allowed to submit bids or proposals on the contract in question.
(2) Public Notice: Public notice of prequalification shall be given in the same manner as provided in section 4-3302 (Competitive sealed bidding, public notice).
(3) Prequalification standards: When the purchasing agent determines that prequalification standards shall be required, those standards shall include but not be limited to the evaluation factors set forth in section 4-3302 (Competitive sealed bidding, award).
(4) Prequalification: The purchasing agent and other affected city departments shall review all information submitted by contractors; and, if necessary, additional information may be required. If the purchasing agent, in consultation with the using department determines that the contractor meets all of the prequalification standards established under this ordinance, then the purchasing agent shall prequalify the contractor as qualified to submit a bid or proposal. The contractor shall be notified in writing of prequalification.
(5) Failure to prequalify: If a contractor is found not to meet the prequalification standards established under this chapter, a written determination setting forth the basis for such finding shall be prepared by the purchasing agent. A notice of failure to prequalify shall be sent to the contractor, which notice shall inform the contractor of the reasons for the failure to prequalify and the steps necessary to cure the failure.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
512:
(1) Required submissions relating to the award of contracts: A prospective contractor shall submit cost or pricing data when the contract is expected to exceed fifty thousand dollars ($50,000.00) and is to be awarded by section 4-3302 (Competitive sealed proposals), by authority of section 4-3305 (Sole source procurement), or by section 4-3307 (Competitive selection procedures for professional and consultant services).
(2) Exceptions: The submission of cost or pricing data relating to the award of a contract is not required where:
(a) The contract price is based on adequate price competition;
(b) The contract price is set by law or regulation; or
(c) It is determined in writing by the purchasing agent that the requirements of section 4-3314 may be waived, and the determination states the reasons for such waiver.
(3) Required submissions relating to change orders or contract modifications: A contractor shall submit cost or pricing data prior to the pricing of any change order or contract modification, including adjustments to contracts awarded by competitive sealed bidding, whether or not cost or pricing data were required in connection with the initial pricing of the contract, when the modification involves aggregate increases in costs plus applicable profits that are expected to exceed five thousand dollars ($5,000.00).
(4) Exceptions: The submission of cost or pricing data relating to the pricing of a change order or contract modification is not required where:
(a) Unrelated and separately priced adjustments for which cost or pricing data would not be required are consolidated for administrative convenience; or
(b) It is determined in writing by the purchasing agent that the requirements of provision (1) of this section may be waived, and the determination states the reasons for such waiver.
(5) Certification required: A contractor, required to submit cost or pricing data in accordance with this section, shall certify that, to the best of its knowledge and belief, the cost or pricing data submitted was accurate, complete and current as of a mutually specified date prior to the award of the contract or the pricing of the change order or contract modification.
(6) Price adjustment provision required: Any contract award, change order or contract modification under which the submission and certification of cost or pricing data are required shall contain a provision stating that the price to the city, including a profit or fee, shall be adjusted to exclude any costs found by the city to have been increased because the contractor-furnished cost or pricing data was inaccurate, incomplete or not current as of the date agreed upon between the city and the contractor.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
513:
If a contract is being funded in whole or in part by assistance from a federal agency, a cost analysis or a price analysis, as appropriate, shall be conducted prior to award of the contract. A written record of such cost analysis or price analysis shall be made a part of the contract file.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
514:
(1) General authority: Subject to the limitations of this section, any type of contract which is appropriate to the procurement and which will promote the best interests of the city may be used; except that the use of a "cost plus a percentage of construction cost" contract is prohibited. A "cost reimbursement" contract may be used only when the purchasing agent determines in writing that such contract is likely to be less costly to the city than any other type or that it is a professional or consultant service contract.
(2) Multi-term contracts.
(a) Specified period. Unless otherwise provided by law, a contract for equipment, supplies or services may be entered into for any period of time deemed to be in the best interests of the city, provided the term of the contract and conditions of renewal or extension, if any, are included in the solicitation and funds are available for the first fiscal period at the time of contracting. Payment and performance obligations for succeeding fiscal periods shall be subject to the availability and appropriation of funds therefor and shall comply with applicable laws.
(b) Determination prior to use. Prior to the utilization of a multi-term contract, it shall be determined in writing:
(i) That estimated requirements cover the period of the contract and are reasonably firm and continuing; and,
(ii) That such a contract will serve the best interests of the city by encouraging effective competition or otherwise promoting economies in city procurement.
(c) Cancellation due to unavailability of funds in succeeding fiscal periods. When funds are not appropriated or otherwise made available to support continuation of performance in a subsequent fiscal period, the contract shall be cancelled. The cost of cancellation may be paid from any appropriations available for such purposes.
(3) Multiple source contracting.
(a) General. A multiple source award is an award of an indefinite quantity contract for one or more similar supplies or services to more than one bidder or offeror. The obligation to order the city's actual requirements is limited to such requirements as may occur in good faith pursuant to O.C.G.A. Section 2-306(1).
(b) Limitations on use. A multiple source award may be made when award to two (2) or more bidders or offerors for similar products is necessary for adequate delivery service or product compatibility. Any multiple source award shall be made in accordance with the provisions of Section 4-3302 (Competitive sealed bidding), Section 4-3303 (Competitive sealed proposals), Section 4-3304 (Small purchases), and Section 4-3306 (Emergency procurements), as applicable. Multiple source awards shall not be made when a single award will meet the city's needs without sacrifice of economy or service. Awards shall not be made for the purpose of dividing the business, making available product or supplier selection to allow for user preference unrelated to utility or economy, or avoiding the resolution of tie bids. Any such awards shall be limited to the least number of suppliers necessary to meet the requirements of this section.
(c) Contract and solicitation provisions. All eligible users of the contract shall be identified in the solicitation, and it shall be mandatory that the actual requirements of such users that can be met under the contract be obtained in accordance with the contract, provided that:
(i) The city shall reserve the right to take bids separately if a particular quantity requirement arises which exceeds its normal requirement or an amount specified in the contract; and,
(ii) The city shall reserve the right to take bids separately if the purchasing agent approves a finding that the supply or service available under the contract will not meet a nonrecurring special need of the city.
(d) Intent to use. If a multiple source award is anticipated prior to issuing a solicitation, the city shall reserve the right to make such an award and the criteria for the award shall be stated in the solicitation.
(e) Determination required. The purchasing agent shall make a written determination setting forth the reasons for a multiple source award, which shall be made a part of the procurement file.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
515:
(1) Extension: The purchasing agent may extend a contract once for ninety (90) days after the date of expiration under the contract, when the following conditions are met:
(a) The purchasing agent determines in writing that the extension of the contract is in the best interests of the city and would encourage effective competition;
(b) The city council, by duly enacted legislation, authorizes and appropriates funds for the extension; and
(c) The city treasurer verifies the availability of funds.
(2) Expiration: The purchasing agent shall provide written notice of the expiration date of contracts to the using department and to the city council at least ninety (90) days prior to the expiration date of the contracts.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
516:
Except with respect to firm fixed-priced contracts, no contract type shall be used unless it has been determined in writing by the purchasing agent that:
(1) The proposed contractor's accounting system will permit timely development of all necessary cost data in the form required by the specified contract type contemplated; and
(2) The proposed contractor's accounting system is adequate to allocate costs in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
517:
The city may, at reasonable times, inspect the part of the plant, place of business, or worksite of a contractor or subcontractor which is pertinent to the performance of any contract awarded or to be awarded by the city.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
518:
(1) Audit of cost or pricing data: The city may, at reasonable times and places, audit the books and records of any person who has submitted cost or pricing data pursuant to this section to the extent that such books, documents, papers and records are pertinent to such cost or pricing data for three years from the date of final payment under the contract unless a shorter period is authorized in writing.
(2) Contract audit: The city shall be entitled to audit the books and records of a contractor or subcontractor under any negotiated contract or subcontract other than a firm fixed-price contract to the extent that such books, documents, papers and records relate to the performance of such contract or subcontract. Such books and records shall be maintained by the contractor for a period of three (3) years from the date of final payment under the prime contract and by the subcontractor for a period of three (3) years from the date of final payment under the subcontract unless a shorter period is authorized in writing.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
519:
Collusion and other anticompetitive practices among bidders and offerors are prohibited by city, state and federal laws. When, for any reason, collusion or other anticompetitive practices are suspected among any bidders or offerors, a notice of the relevant facts shall be transmitted to the city attorney for investigation.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
520:
(1) Requirement: Before final payment to a contractor is made by the city, the contractor shall provide, in a form satisfactory to the city, that all subcontractors and material suppliers involved in the execution of the city contract, have been paid in full at the time of final payment to the contractor by the city.
(2) Contract clause: All city contracts, purchase orders or solicitations, where applicable, shall set forth the requirement of assurance of payment as provided in subsection (1) of this section.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
521:
A contract may be awarded without notice and/or solicitation when the purchasing agent determines that the use of an aggregated purchasing group is appropriate. Only aggregated purchasing groups that utilize an open solicitation process may be used. Any contract awarded via such procedure shall require approval by the city council.
(Ord. No. 034-015, 8-17-15))
522:
(1) Policy. The city has a significant interest in encouraging the creation of employment opportunities for its residents and for businesses located within the city. As a purchaser of goods and services, the city will benefit from expanded job and business opportunities for its residents and businesses through additional revenues generated by its activities. It is in the interest of the city and its residents to give preference on eligible local projects to those eligible offerors who have direct physical and economic relationships with the city.
(2) Definition: A "local vendor" or "local business" means any corporation, partnership, sole proprietorship, franchise, or other business form which:
(a) Has its headquarters, distribution point, retail location, locally-owned franchise, or place of business within the territorial limits of the city, where work and business is and has been regularly conducted for at least six (6) months immediately prior to the issuance of the request for competitive proposals by the city; and
(b) Holds all business or professional licenses required by state law, county ordinance, and city ordinance at the location within the city for at least six (6) months immediately prior to the issuance of the request for competitive proposals by the city.
(3) Application of local preference to specific procurement activity: In an effort to nurture small and large businesses, create jobs, boost local economic activity, and tax revenue, the city will grant the lesser of a five-percent or five-point local preference to all otherwise responsive and responsible vendors who have an actual physical presence and direct economic relationship within the city. This provision is applicable only to the city's acquisition of materials, equipment, or services through the request for proposal (RFP) or request for qualification (RFQ) process as provided in code sections 4-3303, 4-3307, and 4-3313.
(4) Method of granting local preference:
(a) Each corporation, partnership, sole proprietorship, franchise, or other business form seeking local preference points under this section shall certify under oath that it is eligible to receive the local preference points as set forth above as a part of the submission of its proposal or bid to the city and, in the event the affidavit or other declaration under oath is determined to be false, such business shall be deemed "non-responsive" and shall not be considered for award of the applicable contract by the manager of contracts and procurement.
(b) Any local vendor who has been determined by the manager of contracts and procurement to be otherwise responsive and responsible, which also provides proof of its local status under oath will receive the lesser of a five-percent or five-point preference on its total evaluated score.
(5) Local preference shall not apply to the following:
(a) Procurement methods other than a request for proposal (RFP) or request for qualification (RFQ) process as provided in section 4-3303, 4-3307, and 4-3313; or
(b) Procurements for which state or federal law, federal grant provisions, or other funding source prohibits granting a local vendor preference; or
(c) Goods and services provided under a cooperative purchasing agreement or piggyback contracts; or
(d) Emergency, and single or sole source procurement.
(Ord. No. 043-015, 11-2-15)
525:
(1) Brand name specification: A specification limited to one (1) or more items by manufacturers' names or catalogue numbers.
(2) Brand name or equal specification: A specification limited to one (1) or more items by manufacturers' names or catalogue numbers to describe the standard of quality, performance and other salient characteristics needed to meet city requirements, and which provides for the submission of equivalent products.
(3) Specification: Any description of the physical or functional characteristics or of the nature of a supply, service or construction item. It may include a description of any requirement for inspecting, testing or preparing a supply, service or construction item for delivery.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
526:
All specifications shall be drafted so as to promote overall economy for the purposes intended and to encourage competition in satisfying the city's needs, and shall not be unduly restrictive. The policy enunciated in this article applies to all specifications.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
527:
(1) Use: Brand name specification may be used only when the purchasing agent makes a written determination that only the identified brand name item or items will satisfy the city's needs.
(2) Competition: The purchasing agent shall seek to identify sources from which the designated brand name item or items can be obtained and shall solicit such sources to achieve whatever degree of price competition is practicable. If only one source can supply the requirement, the procurement shall be made under section 4-3305 (Sole source procurement).
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
528:
(1) Use: Brand name or equal specification may be used when the purchasing agent determines in writing that:
(a) No other design or performance specification or qualified products list is available;
(b) Time does not permit the preparation of another form of purchase description, not including a brand name specification;
(c) The nature of the product or the nature of the city's requirements makes use of a brand name or equal specification suitable for the procurement; or
(d) Use of a brand name or equal specification is in the city's best interest.
Provided, that the purchasing agent determines that the essential characteristics of the brand name included in the specifications are commonly known in the industry or trade; brand name or equal specifications shall include a description of the particular design, function or performance characteristics which are required.
(2) Designation of several brand names: Brand name or equal specifications shall seek to designate three (3), or as many different brands as are practicable, as "or equal" references and shall further state that substantially equivalent products to those designated will be considered for award.
(3) Nonrestrictive use of brand name or equal specifications: Where a brand name or equal specification is used in a solicitation, the solicitation shall contain explanatory language that the use of a brand name is for the purpose of describing the standard of quality, performance and characteristics desired and is not intended to limit or restrict competition.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
531:
(1) Architect-engineer and land surveying services: Those professional services within the scope of the practice of architecture, professional engineering, land surveying, landscape architecture and interior design pertaining to construction, as defined by the laws of the State of Georgia.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
532:
The using department, at the time the construction project is being developed, shall provide the purchasing agent with information for the scheduling of the project and, if necessary, for the method of selection of architect-engineer and land surveying services, construction services and construction management of the project. In determining which method to use for the selection of architect-engineering and land surveying services, construction services and construction management, the purchasing agent shall consider the city's requirements, its resources and the potential contractor's capabilities. The methods chosen shall be those which are most advantageous to the city and which will result in the most competitive, timely, economical and successful completion of the construction project.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
533:
The purchasing agent, with the assistance of the using department and other appropriate city departments, shall establish the standards for a contract administration system designed to ensure that a contractor is performing in accordance with the solicitation under which the contract is awarded and the terms and conditions of the contract. Such system shall require the inclusion of receiving reports from all appropriate agencies in the contract file.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
534:
(1) Requirement for bid security: Bid security shall be required for all competitive sealed bidding for construction contracts when the price is estimated by the purchasing agent to exceed fifty thousand dollars ($50,000.00). Bid security shall be a bond provided by a surety company authorized to do business in the State of Georgia, or the equivalent in cash, certified check, letter of credit or otherwise supplied in a form satisfactory to the city. Nothing herein prevents the requirement of such bonds on construction contracts under fifty thousand dollars ($50,000.00) when the circumstances warrant.
(2) Amount of bid security: Bid security shall be in an amount equal to at least five (5) percent of the amount of the bid. Unsuccessful bidders shall be entitled to the return of the bid security. Upon failure of a successful bidder to enter into a contract within ten (10) days after the city tenders the proposed contract, the bidder shall forfeit the bid security.
(3) Rejection of bids for noncompliance with the bid security requirements: When the invitation for bids requires security, the bid shall be rejected if the purchasing agent determines that it fails to comply in a substantial manner with the security requirements.
(4) Withdrawal of bids: After the bids are opened, they shall be irrevocable for the period specified in the invitation for bids, except as provided in section 4-3302(9) (Competitive sealed bidding, correction or withdrawal of bids). If a bidder is permitted to withdraw its bid before award, no action shall be had against the bidder or bid security.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
535:
(1) When required—amounts: When a construction contract is awarded in excess of one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000.00), the following bonds or security shall be delivered to the city and shall become binding on the parties upon the execution of the contract:
(a) A performance bond satisfactory to the city, executed by a surety company authorized to do business in the State of Georgia or otherwise secured in a manner satisfactory to the city, in an amount equal to one hundred (100) percent of the price specified in the contract; and
(b) A payment bond satisfactory to the city, executed by a surety company authorized to do business in the State of Georgia or otherwise secured in a manner satisfactory to the city, for the protection of all persons supplying labor and material to the contractor or its subcontractors for the performance of the work provided for in the contract. The bond shall be in an amount equal to one hundred (100) percent of the price specified in the contract.
(2) Reduction or waiver of bond: The purchasing agent is authorized to reduce or waive performance and payment bonds for contracts for one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000.00) or less, when a written determination is made that it is in the best interests of the city to do so. Nothing herein prevents the requirement of such bonds on construction contracts for one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000.00) or less when the circumstances warrant.
(3) Authority to require additional bonds: Nothing in this section shall be construed to limit the authority of the purchasing agent to require a performance bond or other security in addition to those bonds, or in circumstances other than those specified in subsections (1) and (2) of this section.
(4) Suits on payment bonds: Any person who has furnished labor or material to the contractor for the work provided in the contract, for which a payment bond is furnished under this section, and who has not been paid in full within ninety (90) days from the date on which that person performed the last of the labor or supplied the material, shall have the right to sue, as provided in section 4-3311(4) and (5), on the payment bond for any amount unpaid at the time the suit is instituted and to prosecute the action for the amount due that person.
(5) Retention:
(a) Maximum amount to be withheld: In any contract or subcontract for construction which provides for progress payments in installments based upon an estimated percentage of completion with a percentage of the contract's proceeds to be retained by the city pending completion of the contract or subcontract, the retained amount of each progress payment or installment shall be no more than ten (10) percent.
(b) Release of retained funds: Funds held by the city as retainage under the contract shall be released to the contractor as specified in the contract.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
536:
(1) Bond forms: The form of payment and performance bonds shall be prescribed by the purchasing agent, in consultation with the city attorney. The purchasing agent shall designate the bond forms to be used for a particular contract.
(2) Bond copies: Any person may request and obtain from the city a copy of the bond form upon payment of the cost of reproduction and postage.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
537:
Architect-engineer and land surveying services shall be procured as provided in section 4-3307 (Competitive selection procedures for professional and consultant services), except as provided in section 4-3305 (Sole source procurement) and section 4-3306 (Emergency procurement).
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
541:
The purchasing agent, after consultation with and approval by the city attorney, may establish standard contract clauses for use in city contracts. If the purchasing agent establishes any standard clauses addressing the subjects set forth in subsection (1) of this section, such clauses may be varied provided that any variations are supported by a written determination that states the circumstances justifying such variations and provided that notice of any such material variation be stated in the invitation for bids or request for proposals. Any such variations must, however, be approved by the city attorney.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
542:
All contracts, letters of engagement or agreements for equipment, supplies, services, construction services, professional services and consultant services resulting from the bid/procurement process must be approved by council before being executed by the purchasing agent and mayor. Council will approve such contract if they meet the scope of work bid out and the price of the accepted bid.
(Ord. No. 011-03, § 1, 3-3-03)
545:
(1) Excess supplies: Any supplies other than expendable supplies having a remaining useful life but which are no longer required by the using agency in possession of the supplies.
(2) Expendable supplies: All tangible supplies other than nonexpendable supplies.
(3) Nonexpendable supplies: All tangible supplies having an original acquisition cost of over one hundred dollars ($100.00) per unit and a probable useful life of more than one (1) year.
(4) Supplies: For the purpose of this article, supplies owned by the city.
(5) Surplus supplies: Any supplies other than expendable supplies no longer having any use to the city. This includes obsolete supplies, scrap materials, and nonexpendable supplies that have completed their useful life cycle.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
546:
(1) Duties of the purchasing agent: The purchasing agent shall be responsible for:
(a) The sale, lease or disposal of surplus supplies by public auction, competitive sealed bidding or other appropriate method in the best interests of the city, provided that no employee of the owning or disposing using department shall be entitled to purchase such supplies; and
(b) The transfer of excess supplies to using agencies of the city.
(2) Policies and procedures: Consistent with this chapter and with the approval of the city manager and adoption by the city council, the purchasing agent shall develop operational procedures relating to supplies owned by the city during their entire life cycle. These procedures shall be set forth in a purchasing manual and shall promote the objectives of city supply management, which include: preventing waste, continuing utilization of supplies; and obtaining a fair return of value upon disposal of supplies. The procedures adopted shall provide for inspection, testing, warehousing, inventory and effective transfer and disposition of supplies.
(3) Requirement upon using departments: No using department shall transfer, sell, trade in, or otherwise dispose of supplies owned by the city without written notification to the purchasing agent, and in accordance with property disposition procedures.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
547:
The purchasing agent, in consultation with the using department, shall ascertain or verify that equipment, supplies, services, construction or professional and consultant services procured for the city conform to specifications. The purchasing agent may establish inspection or testing facilities, employ inspection personnel, enter into arrangements for the joint or cooperative use of inspection and testing facilities, and contract with others for inspection and testing work as needed.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
548:
The purchasing agent shall exercise general supervision of all inventory of supplies, whether warehoused or in use, belonging to the city or any of its departments. The department, however, shall maintain an inventory of supplies under its control. All warehouses and similar storage areas shall be inventoried at least annually by each department, a written report of which shall be submitted to the purchasing agent and to the city manager accounting for inventory.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
549:
The purchasing agent shall exercise general supervision of any receiving, storage, and distribution facilities and services of the city maintained and operated by the purchasing department.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
550:
Using departments shall notify the purchasing agent, at prescribed times, of all excess supplies. The purchasing agent shall transfer excess supplies to other city agencies as determined by need and in accordance with operational procedures adopted pursuant to this chapter.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
551:
(1) General requirements: Unless otherwise provided, the purchasing agent shall dispose of any supplies owned by the city, upon the recommendation of and after consultation with the department, as herein provided. Surplus supplies which have an estimated value in excess of five hundred dollars ($500.00) shall be offered through competitive sealed bids or public auction. Surplus supplies which have an estimated value of five hundred dollars ($500.00) or less may be offered by established markets, posted prices, or by any other means advantageous to the city. The purchasing agent shall determine the estimated value of the surplus property to be sold. Notwithstanding the above, the purchasing agent may exchange or trade in surplus supplies with another property owner if such exchange or trade is deemed to be in the best interests of the city.
(2) Competitive sealed bidding:
(a) Solicitation and opening: When making sales of surplus supplies by competitive sealed bidding, notice of the sale shall be given by advertisement in a newspaper of general circulation at least once no less than fifteen (15) nor more than sixty (60) days before the date set for receipt of bids. Notice may also be given by mailing an invitation for sale bids to prospective bidders, including those bidders on lists maintained for this purpose, and by making invitation for sale bids publicly available. The invitation for sale bids shall list the supplies offered for sale, designate their location and how they may be inspected, and state the terms and conditions of sale and instructions to bidders, including the place, date and time for bid opening. Bids shall be opened publicly.
(b) Award: Award shall be made in accordance with the provisions of the invitation for sale bids to the highest responsible bidder, provided that the price offered by such bidder is acceptable to the purchasing agent. Where such price is not acceptable, the purchasing agent may reject the bids in whole or in part and negotiate the sale provided the negotiated sale price is higher than the highest responsive and responsible bidder's price, or such officer may resolicit bids.
(3) Auctions: Supplies may be sold at public auction. Notice of such auction shall be given by advertisement in a newspaper of general circulation at least once no less than fifteen (15) nor more than sixty (60) days before the day of the auction. When appropriate, an experienced auctioneer should be used to cry the sale and assist in preparation of the sale. The notice shall contain a general description of the property to be sold, all the terms and conditions of the sale, that a deposit may be required in order to participate in the bidding, that the purchaser must remove within a stated time all surplus supplies purchased, and that the city retains the right to reject any and all bids.
(4) Established markets, posted prices and trade-in: Surplus supplies which have an estimated value of five hundred dollars ($500.00) or less may be sold in established markets where such supplies, including but not limited to livestock and produce, are regularly sold in wholesale lots and prices are set by open competition. Surplus supplies may be sold at posted prices as determined by the purchasing agent, provided that such prices are based on fair market value and the sale is conducted pursuant to procedures established under this article. Surplus supplies may be traded in only when the purchasing agent determines that the trade-in value is expected to exceed the value estimated to be obtained through the sale or other disposition of such supplies.
(5) Payment for surplus supplies: Only United States postal money orders, certified checks, and cashier's checks shall be accepted for sales of surplus property, except cash or a personal check may be accepted for petty cash sales of less than one hundred dollars ($100.00). A copy of all sales notices or invoices shall be sent to the city treasurer.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
552:
Upon completion of sale, lease or disposal of surplus or excess property owned by the city, the purchasing agent shall notify the commissioner of the department of finance in writing, which notice shall contain, at a minimum, a description of the property sold, the inventory control number, the amount for which the article was sold, and the using department in which the property was used. The city treasurer shall make the necessary corrections to the inventory of the city. The purchasing agent shall pay the proceeds of such sales, lease or disposal of property owned by the city to the city treasurer, as required by law.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
555:
(1) Right to protest: Any actual or prospective bidder, offeror, contractor or subcontractor who is aggrieved in connection with the prequalification, solicitation or award of a contract shall protest to the purchasing agent. Protestors are urged to seek resolution of their complaints initially with the purchasing agent. A protest with respect to an invitation for bids or request for proposals shall be submitted to the purchasing agent in writing within five (5) calendar days after such aggrieved person knows or should have known of the facts giving rise thereto, but in no circumstance after five (5) calendar days of notification of award of contract.
(2) Authority to resolve protests: The purchasing agent shall have authority, prior to protest to the city manager, to settle and resolve a protest of an aggrieved bidder, offeror, contractor or subcontractor, actual or prospective, concerning the prequalification, solicitation or award of a contract.
(3) Decision: If a written protest is submitted, the purchasing agent shall inform the protestant of the decision in writing within seven (7) calendar days. The decision of the purchasing agent shall state the reasons for the action taken and inform the protestant of the right to review by the city manager as provided in this article.
(4) Finality of decision: A decision under subsection (3) of this section is final and conclusive, unless fraudulent, or any person adversely affected by the decision appeals to the city council in accordance with this article.
(5) Finality of city manager's decision; contractor's right to appeal: The city manager's decision shall be final and conclusive unless, within seven (7) calendar days from the date of receipt of the decision, the contractor mails or otherwise delivers a written appeal to the city council or commences an action in a court of competent jurisdiction.
(6) Failure to render timely decision: If the city manager does not issue a written decision regarding any contract controversy within ten (10) calendar days after written request for a final decision, or within such longer period as may be agreed upon between the parties, then the aggrieved party may proceed as if an adverse decision had been received.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
556:
(1) Applicability: This section applies where it is determined by administrative review, that a solicitation or award of a contract is in violation of law.
(2) Remedies prior to award: If prior to award the purchasing agent, after consultation with the city attorney, determines that a solicitation or proposed award of a contract is in violation of law, then the solicitation or proposed award shall be cancelled or revised to comply with the law.
(3) Remedies after award: If after an award the purchasing agent, after consultation with the city attorney, determines that a solicitation or award of a contract is in violation of applicable law, then:
(a) If the person awarded the contract has not acted fraudulently or in bad faith:
(i) The contract may be ratified and affirmed, provided it is determined that so doing is in the best interest of the city; or
(ii) The contract may be terminated and the person awarded the contract shall be compensated for the actual expenses reasonably incurred under the contract, plus a reasonable profit, prior to the termination;
(b) If the person awarded the contract has acted fraudulently or in bad faith:
(i) The contract may be declared null and void or voidable; or
(ii) The contract may be ratified and affirmed if such action is in the best interests of the city, without prejudice to the city's right to such damages as may be appropriate.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
559:
The city council, by a duly enacted resolution, may reject a bid, offer or other response to the city solicitation, or cancel any contract, because of any false representation contained in or made in conjunction with an invitation for bids, request for proposals, or any other solicitation of the city.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
560:
It shall be unethical for any city employee to participate directly or indirectly in a procurement contract when the city employee knows that:
(a) The city employee or any members of the city employee's family has a financial interest pertaining to the procurement contract; or,
(b) Any other person, business, or organization with whom the city employee or any member of a city employee's immediate family is negotiating or has an arrangement concerning prospective employment is involved in the procurement contract.
A city employee or any member of a city employee's immediate family who holds a financial interest in a disclosed blind trust shall be not deemed to have a conflict of interest with regard to matters pertaining to that financial interest.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
561:
(1) Gratuities: It shall be unethical for any person to offer, give or agree to give any employee or former employee, or for any employee or former employee to solicit, demand, accept or agree to accept from another person a gratuity or an offer of employment in connection with any decision, approval, disapproval, recommendation, preparation or any part of a program requirement or a purchase request, influencing the content of any specification or procurement standard, rendering of advice, investigation, auditing, or in any other advisory capacity in any proceeding or application, request for ruling, determination, claim or controversy, or other particular matter, pertaining to any program requirement or a contract or subcontract, or to any solicitation or proposal therefor.
(2) Kickbacks: It shall be unethical for any payment, gratuity or offer of employment to be made by or on behalf of a subcontractor under a contract to the prime contractor or higher tier subcontractor or any person associated therewith, as an inducement for the award of a subcontract or order.
(3) Contract clause: The prohibition against gratuities and kickbacks prescribed in this section shall be conspicuously set forth in every contract and solicitation therefor.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
562:
(1) Prohibition against contingent fees: It shall be unethical for a person to be retained, or to retain a person, to solicit or secure a city contract upon an agreement or understanding for a commission, percentage, brokerage or contingent fee, except for retention of bona fide employees of bona fide established commercial selling agencies for the purpose of securing business.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
563:
Unless otherwise provided herein, it shall be unethical under this article for any employee who is participating directly or indirectly in the procurement process to become or to be, while such an employee, the employee of any person contracting with the governmental body by whom the employee is employed.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
564:
In accordance with this article, it shall be unethical for any employee or former employee willfully to use confidential information for actual or anticipated personal gain, or for the actual or anticipated personal gain of any other person.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
565:
(1) Criminal penalties: To the extent that violations of the ethical standards of conduct set forth in this article constitute violations of the Georgia State Code, or violations of the city standards of conduct, they shall be punishable as provided therein. Such penalties shall be in addition to the civil sanctions set forth in this article. Criminal, civil and administrative sanctions against employees or nonemployees which are in existence on the effective date of this ordinance shall not be impaired.
(2) Sanctions:
(a) Employees: The city manager may impose any one (1) or more of the following sanctions on an employee for violations of the ethical standards contained in this article:
(i) Oral or written warnings or reprimands;
(ii) Suspension with or without pay for specified periods of time; or
(iii) Termination of employment.
(b) Nonemployees: The city council may impose any one (1) or more of the following sanctions on a nonemployee for violations of the ethical standards:
(i) Written warnings or reprimands;
(ii) Termination of contracts; or
(iii) Debarment or suspension in the city's bidding and contracting processes.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
566:
(1) General requirement: The value of anything transferred or received in breach of the ethical standards of this chapter by an employee or a nonemployee may be recovered from both the employee and nonemployee.
(2) Recovery of kickbacks by the city: Upon a showing that a subcontractor made a kickback to a prime contractor or a higher tier subcontractor in connection with the award of a subcontract or order thereunder, it shall be conclusively presumed that the amount thereof was included in the price of the subcontract or order and ultimately borne by the city and will be recoverable hereunder from the recipient. In addition, that amount may also be recovered from the subcontractor making such kickbacks. Recovery from one offending party shall not preclude recovery from other offending parties.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)
567:
Unless otherwise provided by law, when sanctions are imposed under this article, the city manager shall give written notice to the offending party, by registered or certified mail, which notice shall state the reasons therefor and effective date, and shall notify the offending party of the right to protest and appeal to the city council as provided in Article H (Appeals and Remedies) of this chapter.
(Ord. No. 1111-95, § 1, 7-3-95)

Mediation means a process whereby a neutral third person called a "mediator" acts to encourage and facilitate the resolution of a dispute between two (2) or more parties. (1) Agricultural use and service tax district.
a. Defined. Agricultural use and service tax district shall be an area determined by the city council to fall within this category and shall be predominated, used and developed for agricultural purposes and the ancillary and necessary services in support thereof. Such agricultural uses shall include but not necessarily be limited to planting, cultivation and growth of forests for timber, pulpwood and other forest products, dairy and beef cattle farm operations, planting, cultivation and harvesting of row crops and including growth, cultivation and harvesting of hay. Use for the purposes of mining or quarrying of any type is excluded from agricultural use for the purposes of this section. The predominant determination of this category shall be that the use and any and all products derived from such areas shall be a product of the land and earth upon which it is situated. The ancillary and incidental uses thereto shall include residence of the owner or operator and living quarters of support personnel, together with structures used directly in support of the predominant agricultural use. Such area, because of its rural and predominant agricultural use, shall require minimal police and fire services. This classification shall be deemed to be abandoned when any additional development inconsistent with its predominant agricultural use is undertaken as may be evidenced by the request or furnishing of any of the following utility services, including but not limited to sewage collection system, water distribution system, storm drainage system or additional read [road] installation. Any application for rezoning other than for agricultural use shall be prima facie evidence of abandonment of the agricultural use and service tax district.
b. Tax schedule.
1. There shall be no ad valorem tax imposed by the City of East Point upon land classified in the agricultural use and service tax district for the tax year commencing January 1 following the annexation of such area.
2. Commencing January 1 of the second year after annexation of any area within this classification, there shall be imposed thereon an ad valorem tax as above stated equivalent to twenty-five (25) percent of the millage applicable to full service tax districts of the City of East Point.
3. Commencing January 1 of the third year after annexation of any area within this classification, there shall be imposed thereon an ad valorem tax as above stated equivalent to forty (40) percent of the millage applicable to full service tax districts of the City of East Point.
4. Commencing January 1 of the fourth year after annexation of any area within this classification, there shall be imposed thereon an ad valorem tax as above stated equivalent to fifty (50) percent of the millage applicable to full service tax districts of the City of East Point, and continuing at this level from year to year thereafter until termination of the agricultural use and service tax district.
(2) Developmental use and service tax district.
(a) Defined. Developmental use and service tax district shall be any area annexed to the City of East Point which has been or becomes transitional from a predominant rural and agricultural use to development for residential, commercial or industrial usage. For the purposes of determining developmental classification, it shall be conclusively presumed to be developmental unless already in use for residential, commercial or industrial use when there is filed an application for rezoning for other than agricultural use, or utility services of water distribution, sewage collection, storm sewer drainage or street improvements are permitted and installed upon such property.
(b) Tax schedule.
1. For developmental use and service tax districts so defined upon annexation, the ad valorem tax assessment on such property shall be zero percentage of the city millage for the first year commencing on January 1 after its annexation.
2. On January 1 after becoming classified as developmental use from agricultural use and service tax districts or the second year after annexation and so classified upon annexation, the ad valorem tax imposition against such property shall be fifty (50) percent of the millage imposed upon all full service tax districts of the city.
3. On January 1 of the second year after becoming classified as developmental use from agricultural use and service tax districts or the third year after annexation and so classified upon annexation, the ad valorem tax imposition against such property shall be seventy-five (75) percent of the millage imposed upon all full service tax districts of the city.
4. On January 1 of the third year after becoming classified as developmental use from agricultural use and service tax districts or the fourth year after annexation and so classified upon annexation, the ad valorem tax imposition against such property shall be one hundred (100) percent of the millage imposed upon all full service tax districts of the city.
(3) Full service tax district.
(a) Defined. [A full service tax district shall consist of] all other properties of the City of East Point except agricultural use and service tax districts and developmental use and service tax districts developed for residential, commercial or industrial usage.
(b) Tax schedule. On and after January 1 of the year after annexation, all property not meeting the two (2) preceding categories shall have imposed thereon one hundred (100) percent of the citywide tax millage.
